comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation reports results through four business segments (Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management, Global Banking, and Global Markets) and All Other, managed by the Management Team with the CEO as the Chief Operating Decision Maker for capital allocation.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America define their operating segments and the governance structure for capital allocation, though neither disclosed material segment reclassifications or realignments in 2024. Citi explicitly stated that its consolidated results remained unchanged following significant internal reclassifications of deposit balances and business units (c_2024_8_P195_S001, c_2024_8_P194_S002). In contrast, Bank of America's disclosure focuses on its static four-segment structure and the CEO's role as the Chief Operating Decision Maker for capital allocation, with no mention of structural changes or reallocations affecting segment reporting during the year (bac_2024_8_P559_S001, bac_2024_8_P559_S004).

sentences.text: Citi's consolidated results remain unchanged for all periods presented following the changes and reclassifications discussed above.

The Corporation reports its results of operations through the following four business segments: Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management, Global Banking and Global Markets, with the remaining operations recorded in All Other.

comparisons.peer_topic: Segment accounting policies and allocation methods
comparisons.peer_summary: Accounting policies for segment results are consistent with Note 3, involving full allocation of revenues, expenses, assets, and equity to the three segments, with specific rules for interest income/expense, indirect expense allocation, and segment-level net earnings calculation using the firmwide tax rate.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures detail the accounting policies governing the preparation of segment results, but Citi highlights a revision of those results through reallocation, whereas Goldman Sachs describes the ongoing allocation methodology without noting changes. Citi notes that segment results were revised to reallocate deposit balances and align businesses with strategy, conforming prior periods (c_2024_8_P194_S003). Goldman Sachs describes its consistent accounting policies, including the full allocation of revenues and expenses and the use of estimates for intersegment transfers, which implies a stable methodology compared to Citi's active realignment (gs_2024_8_P634_S001, gs_2024_8_P634_S004).

sentences.text: • Realigned businesses engaged in financing and securitization activities within Banking and Markets, transferred the retail banking business in the U.K., which is being wound down, from Wealth to All Other and made other immaterial reclassifications to align with Citi's transformation and strategy. These reclassifications did not materially change segment or All Other results, and prior periods were conformed to reflect these changes.
The accounting policies used to prepare the operating results and other metrics for the segments are consistent with those described in Note 3.

comparisons.peer_topic: Segment results basis and GAAP reconciliation
comparisons.peer_summary: Segment results on a managed basis reflect revenue on a FTE basis with corresponding tax impact, and these adjustments are eliminated in reconciling items to arrive at the Firm's reported U.S. GAAP results.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the basis of segment results, but Citi focuses on structural reclassifications with no impact on consolidated results, while JPMorgan focuses on tax-based presentation adjustments (FTE) that reconcile to GAAP. Citi states that consolidated results remain unchanged despite segment realignments (c_2024_8_P195_S001). JPMorgan explains that segment results on a managed basis reflect revenue on a full-time equivalent basis, with tax impacts eliminated in reconciling items to arrive at reported U.S. GAAP results, indicating a different type of adjustment (jpm_2024_8_P941_S001, jpm_2024_8_P941_S002).

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm uses an Intersegment Eliminations category to reconcile business segment results to consolidated results, treating inter-segment transactions as external parties for disclosure purposes.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss the mechanics of reconciling segment results to consolidated financial statements. Citi achieves this reconciliation by noting that its internal reclassifications and realignments did not materially change segment or All Other results, leaving consolidated results unchanged (c_2024_8_P194_S004). Morgan Stanley uses a specific 'Intersegment Eliminations' category to reconcile business segment results to consolidated results, treating inter-segment transactions as external parties (ms_2024_8_P578_S001).

sentences.text: • Reallocated certain customer balances between All Other-Legacy Franchises, Services, Markets and Banking in preparation for the IPO of the Mexico Consumer/SBMM operations, and made other immaterial reclassifications. These reallocations and reclassifications did not materially change segment or All Other results, and prior periods were conformed to reflect these changes.

As a result of revenues and expenses from transactions with other operating segments being treated as transactions with external parties for purposes of segment disclosures, the Firm includes an Intersegment Eliminations category to reconcile the business segment results to the consolidated results.
